status: preview: not reviewed by a tax professional for this country

conventions.amounts: decimal strings; quantities in asset units (exact multiples of 1e-11, Kassiber's msat); fiat in the country currency
conventions.times: ISO 8601 with offset; every date rule uses the local date in `timezone`
conventions.expected: the spec's hand-computed results, which scripts/tax-country-vectors.py check recomputes; `rp2.computed` is RP2's plugin on the same inputs

notes: Quantities are decimal strings in asset units (Kassiber stores msat; every quantity here is an exact multiple of 1e-11). Fiat amounts are EUR decimal strings. `expected` follows the rules of the spec; `rp2.computed` is RP2's ES plugin (FIFO) on the same inputs, written by scripts/tax-country-vectors.py; `rp2.differences` explains every gap.

vectors.title: AEAT informador example: FIFO partial lot with purchase and sale commissions

differences: RP2 does not deduct the EUR sale commission (an OutTransaction fiat_fee never reaches proceeds): RP2 gain 7,369.96 against 7,089.96. Art. 35.2 LIRPF deducts it.
Not an RP2 difference: the AEAT informador prints 6,673.36 and 7,092.96, but 3,060.00 + 3,616.36 = 6,676.36, so the correct gain is 7,089.96.

vectors.title: FIFO is global across exchanges and wallets

differences: None. RP2 also pools all of the holder's wallets.

vectors.title: Permuta: the received coins are worth more than those given (art. 37.1.h)

differences: RP2 has no permuta rule: the BTC leg is sold at its own value 30,000 (gain 20,000 against 20,600). The ETH basis is 30,600 in both.

vectors.title: Permuta: the coins given are worth more; the received coins take that higher value as basis

differences: RP2 gives SOL its own value 48,000 as basis instead of the permuta transmission value 50,500, so the SOL sale gains 1,000 instead of losing 1,500; the year nets +1,500 instead of -1,000.

vectors.title: Paying for goods with bitcoin is a permuta at the higher of the goods' and the coins' value

differences: RP2 values the payment at the coins' market value 2,450 (gain 1,450 against 1,500); art. 37.1.h takes the higher of the two values.

vectors.title: Gifts: a gain is taxed at market value, a loss is not computable (arts. 36, 33.5.c)

differences: RP2 counts the loss on the gifted ETH (-1,000); art. 33.5.c LIRPF does not.

vectors.title: Staking rewards are capital-mobiliario yields (casilla 0027); a later loss offsets up to 25 % of them

differences: Disposal identical. RP2 lists the staking reward as a taxable event (gain 1,500) without the casilla 0027 / ahorro classification or the 25 % offset.

vectors.title: Airdrop and hobby mining are general-base gains at market value (casilla 0304) and set the basis

differences: Disposal identical. RP2 lists the airdrop and mining receipts as taxable events without the casilla 0304 / base general classification.

vectors.title: Lending interest is a capital-mobiliario yield (art. 25.2); its casilla is unconfirmed

differences: RP2 lists the interest as a taxable event; it has no casilla.

vectors.title: A network fee on a move between own wallets disposes of the fee coins; the move itself is not taxable

differences: None. RP2 treats the move's fee as a taxable event: 6.00 - 3.00 = 3.00.

vectors.title: A fee paid in bitcoin on a sale: one row disposing of the sold and the fee coins

differences: Same gain (39,960.00). RP2 reports two lot fragments and spreads the proceeds pro rata (59,940.06 + 59.94) instead of one row with transmission value 60,000.

vectors.title: A sale below market value is taxed at market value (art. 35.2)

differences: RP2 takes the agreed price 3,000 (gain 1,000 against 4,000); art. 35.2 substitutes the higher market value.

vectors.title: A loss followed by a repurchase within a year: computed by default, flagged for art. 33.5.e review

differences: None in the numbers. Neither applies art. 33.5.e; Kassiber adds the review flag.

vectors.title: A sale at 00:30 Madrid time on 1 January belongs to the new tax year even though it is 31 December in UTC

differences: RP2 dates the sale 2025 (it reads the year in the timestamp's own offset, here UTC); Kassiber uses Europe/Madrid, so the sale is 2026.

vectors.title: Crypto-only ahorro integration over two years: 25 % offset against staking, then four-year carry-forward

differences: Gains identical. RP2 has no ahorro integration (25 % offset, four-year carry-forward).

vectors.title: Lost or stolen coins are not booked as a loss; Kassiber quarantines them for review (arts. 33.5.a, 14.2.k)

differences: RP2 books LOST as a full capital loss (-4,000.00); Kassiber quarantines (arts. 33.5.a, 14.2.k LIRPF).

vectors.title: A hard fork has no published AEAT treatment; Kassiber quarantines the new coins

differences: RP2 books the fork as HARDFORK income of 300 with basis 300; Kassiber quarantines because AEAT publishes no treatment.
